newsitem.title: UK: S&P affirms Pacific Mutual Life Insurance ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms Pacific Mutual Life Insurance ratings.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it affirmed its AA plus claims-paying ability and issuer credit ratings on Pacific Mutual Life Insurance Co.

"In addition, Standard & Poor's has affirmed its AA minus rating on Pacific Mutual's contribution certificates (surplus notes) and its A1 plus rating on the company's commercial paper," it said in a statement.

"The claims-paying ability rating reflects the company's strong market positions in core businesses, diversified sources of earnings, excellent capitalisation, and solid investment quality," the agency said.
Key rating factors included the following --

-- Pacific Mutual's management has maintained growth in the substantial and profitable book of individual life insurance and group pension business, diversified into faster growing market segments such as individual annuities, and expanded its fee income from assets under management,
-- On a statutory basis, return on assets (excluding capital gains) of 0.67 percent for 1995 is solid given the business mix and double-digit growth,
-- Capitalisation is excellent, with total adjusted capital for Pacific Mutual and its two principal life insurance subsidiaries totaling nearly $1 billion,

-- Pacific Mutual's investments have outperformed much of the life insurance industry, in part due to its concentration in mortgage loans on mobile home parks, which have had low loss experience, while the balance of its investment profile reflects prudent levels of credit quality and interest-rate risk,
-- and while financial flexibility is limited as a mutual company, Pacific Mutual has been able to make acquisitions requiring minimal capital.
S&P said the long-term debt outlook was stable.
"Standard & Poor's expects that growth in Pacific Mutual's core businesses will continue to be robust as the insurer expands and diversifies its distribution channels," it said.
"Statutory return on assets should remain at about the current level because of surplus strain from new business. However, underlying economic earnings are expected to increase," it said.

"Standard & Poor's believes that Pacific Mutual's problem assets will remain at levels that are low compared to industry experience. California's new mutual holding company legislation provides an opportunity for greater financial flexibility," the agency said.
